title: An UpstreamBreak of five or more steps overflows a 360px page
instrument: static HTML with tokens.css + UpstreamBreak.module.css in headless Chromium at 360px (no server), assert rail scrollWidth <= clientWidth for 4/5/6 steps; or cx-capture of the part workspace at --width 360
body:
## Summary
UpstreamBreak nodes hold a 70px min-width in a non-wrapping flex rail, so a chain of 5+ steps overflows a phone page.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/upstream/UpstreamBreak.module.css:5 `.node{--one-off-w-node:70px;min-width:...}` sits in `.rail{display:flex}` with no wrap or shrink. PartWorkspace (packages/ui/src/components/part/PartWorkspace.tsx:79) passes [...upstream, here]: four missing upstream parts make five steps. Fixed looks like nodes that shrink and wrap their words below ~70px, or a rail that wraps with its links; an overflow-x scroller is not it (a scrollable region with no focusable child fails axe scrollable-region-focusable).

## Flow
- headless Chromium, static page, tokens.css + module CSS, 360px viewport, 16px gutter
- 4 steps: 0px; 5 steps: +38px rail / 21px page; 6 steps: +108px / 91px

## Expected impact
A phone reader of a part with many missing upstream parts sees the page scroll sideways. Could break: the 4-step SlotDetail chain at desktop.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no horizontal page overflow at 360px for chains up to 6 steps
Before: 5 steps 21px, 6 steps 91px page overflow
After: not built: 0px expected for a shrink-and-wrap node
Method: probe - Before measured by the probe; the fix is a layout choice (wrap vs shrink) the round did not settle
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The --hatch stripes read 2.5:1 on a StackBar's track, under the 3:1 mark floor
instrument: a Node case over tests/live/_legibility.ts contrastRatio composing the --hatch stripe over --wash-hi over --ink, floor 3, read from source.json
body:
## Summary
StackBar's undecided segment (and an untouched pile, drawn whole-hatched) is --hatch: white .28 stripes on a white .05 track, 2.51:1.

## Description
packages/ui/tokens/source.json:185 --hatch repeating-linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,.28) 0 2px, transparent 2px 5px); packages/ui/src/components/stackbar/StackBar.module.css:6 .undecided{background:var(--hatch)} over .bar background var(--wash-hi). The stripes are what tell undecided from empty, so they carry state (WCAG 1.4.11). tests/live/_legibility.ts does not model gradients, so the lane cannot see it. Out of this context's paths: the token is the tokens context's, and every --hatch user (RunsDayline, LoadBand, ...) moves with it.

## Flow
- composite white .28 over (white .05 over --ink): 2.51:1 against the track; 2.53 on ink-2 / sheet-ground
- raise the stripe alpha until >= 3:1 and recheck every --hatch site

## Expected impact
The untouched pile and the undecided share of a decided pile become visibly hatched. Could break: denser hatch reads heavier in RunsDayline and LoadBand.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every --hatch stripe at >= 3:1 against its track
Before: 2.51:1
After: not built; ~.38 alpha reaches 3:1 by the same arithmetic
Method: probe - WCAG arithmetic on the token values; out of scope (tokens), so not built
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Tally draws raw numerals while three private en-US formatters group them
instrument: a case rendering Tally{value:12345} expecting '12,345', plus a count of toLocaleString/Intl.NumberFormat sites under packages/ui/src == 1
body:
## Summary
Tally renders a number value raw (12345) while floor/slot.ts NUM, library/library.ts count and model/ModelViewer.tsx fmt each group en-US (12,345): no one numeric primitive.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/tally/Tally.tsx:28 renders `value` raw; status-vocabulary / number-formatting asks for one numeric primitive with the locale bound inside it. Three formatters exist privately: packages/ui/src/components/floor/slot.ts:109, packages/ui/src/components/library/library.ts:161, packages/ui/src/components/model/ModelViewer.tsx:63. The registry map already records the deviation (evaluated 2026-10-22). Fixed: one @gt/ui number primitive, Tally formatting a number through it, the three sites adopting it.

## Flow
- Tally{value:12345} -> '12345'; library count(12345) -> '12,345'
- add the primitive, route Tally and the three sites through it, re-run the 45 Tally callers' specs

## Expected impact
Counts past 999 read alike on every surface. Could break: specs asserting a raw numeral in a Tally.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one numeric renderer
Before: 4 renderings (3 private formatters + Tally raw)
After: 1
Method: simulation - walked; it touches files in three other contexts, so the round did not build it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
